result:
Done. `maze.py` is written at the repo root and verified.

## Approach

Every corridor cell is carved as the **perimeter of a rectangle** — a cycle. The union of cycles has minimum degree 2 everywhere, so "no dead ends" holds by construction rather than by retry. Symmetry is an invariant: each cell is carved together with its mirror, so the grid is symmetric at every instant. Connectivity is enforced by requiring each new ring to touch the existing corridor set before it is carved.

Structure: outer ring → castrum ring (rows 14–19 × cols 10–17, exactly the 8-neighbourhood of the solid block) → random 1-wide connectors between the two → full tunnel row → random rings until the density target, biased toward the least-populated regions so the maze doesn't leave large solid blocks.

## Verification

A validator written from the spec text, independent of the generator, over **804 seeds** (−300…500, plus 0, ±2⁶⁴, 123456789): all nine constraints pass, no two seeds produce the same grid, density ranges 0.405–0.532. Output is deterministic across processes under a different `PYTHONHASHSEED`, and `render` returns exactly 36 lines with no trailing newline.

## One thing you should know

Constraints 3, 4 and 7 are **mutually unsatisfiable under a non-wrapping 4-neighbourhood**, and this is provable, not a limitation of my construction: symmetry forces `grid[r][0] == grid[r][27]` (since `27−0 = 27`), so col 0 and col 27 are the same column under mirroring; constraint 7 then allows exactly one corridor cell in col 0, whose vertical neighbours are necessarily wall. Its only in-grid horizontal neighbour is `(r_t,1)` — degree 1. No construction escapes it.

So I implemented the tunnel mouths as joined by horizontal wrap-around (east of col 27 is col 0), which is the adjacency the game actually uses, and noted it in the module docstring. To make the residual as tight as possible, I verified across all 804 seeds that the set of cells failing a **strictly non-wrapping** dead-end test is *exactly* `{(r_t,0), (r_t,27)}` — never anything else. And on your advisor's prompting I re-ran the full validator under non-wrapping adjacency: every other constraint, **including single-component connectivity**, still passes with zero failures. The two tunnel mouths are the only cells that depend on the wrap reading.

Minor defect caught and fixed during testing: CPython's `random.Random(int)` folds the sign, so seeds `1` and `−1` originally produced identical grids, violating constraint 9. Seeds now pass through a bijective zig-zag map to the non-negatives.
